system_type_reason: End-user platform that turns novels into short videos via a fixed orchestrator agent and subagents.

repo_overview.summary: AI video generation platform that turns novels into short videos (narration, drama and ad content modes). A React SPA talks to a FastAPI server that hosts a Claude Agent SDK runtime: an orchestrator agent, driven by a content-mode specific system prompt, calls skills, six subagents and in-process MCP tools, and the MCP tools enqueue image/video/audio generation jobs that a background worker executes against many third-party media providers.

components.purpose: Claude Agent SDK integration: AssistantService and SessionManager (session lifecycle, SDK options, SSE subscribers), SessionActor (one asyncio task per session serializing all ClaudeSDKClient calls), SessionStore (transcript DB mirror), StreamProjector and transcript/turn adapters for live and replayed replies
in-process MCP tools exposed to the agent (enqueue assets/grid/storyboards/videos, text generation), the bridge from agent decisions to the generation queue

agent runtime configuration: CLAUDE.narration/drama/ad.md system prompt variants injected per content_mode, .claude/agents/ with six subagent definitions, .claude/skills/ with nine workflow skills (script, assets, storyboard, grid, video, audio, compose, project management) and their scripts
FastAPI /api/v1 endpoints: assistant/agent chat (SSE), generation enqueueing, tasks, projects and asset CRUD, versions/rollback, usage and cost estimation, provider and credential configuration, auth

topology.justification: The main agent has the Task tool enabled (session_manager.py:318-320) and loads project settings (session_manager.py:333), through which the SDK picks up the six subagent definitions in .claude/agents/ that the profile sync copies into each project. The mode-specific CLAUDE.md defines the main agent as a lightweight orchestrator that holds only project state and user dialogue and dispatches analyze-assets, split-narration-segments, normalize-drama-script, split-reference-video-units, create-episode-script and generate-assets (CLAUDE.narration.md:79-89). Each subagent has its own system prompt and role (e.g. create-episode-script.md:1-8, which also preloads the generate-script skill), runs in its own context, finishes one focused task and returns a summary; subagents cannot spawn further subagents, so multi-step work is chained by the orchestrator (CLAUDE.narration.md:101-103). This is a two-level orchestrator-worker hierarchy of LLM agents.

resilience.name: JSON write guard with pre-check and rollback
resilience.what_it_is: A PreToolUse hook on Write/Edit targeting .json files simulates the resulting file content (Edit: string replacement on the current file) and validates it with json.loads; invalid results and curly quotes in new_string are denied with a correction hint. The pre-hook stores a backup of the file keyed by tool_use_id. A PostToolUse hook re-validates the written file, restores the backup if it is invalid JSON and returns additionalContext telling the agent the file was rolled back.
resilience.function_in_system: Sits around the agent's built-in Write/Edit tool calls inside the SDK tool loop. Project state (project.json, episode scripts, drafts) lives in JSON files that every later step and the generation worker read. The deny reason and the additionalContext feed back into the conversation so the agent retries with corrected input. Otherwise a single malformed edit corrupts a project file and breaks all downstream skills and generation tasks.

resilience.name: path-based tool access fence
resilience.what_it_is: A PreToolUse hook fires for every Read/Write/Edit/Glob/Grep call and checks the resolved path: sensitive files (.env, DB, system config, vertex_keys, logs, agent settings.json) are always denied; reads outside the current project, the SDK temp outputs and the repo reference docs are denied; writes are restricted to the project cwd, code file extensions are denied, and scripts/*.json plus project.json are denied with a message that names the MCP tools to use instead.
resilience.function_in_system: Step 1 of the SDK permission chain, so it overrides allow rules for all built-in file tools. Contains the agent to its own project and keeps it away from credentials. The deny reasons are returned to the agent as tool feedback and redirect structured edits to the validated MCP tools. Otherwise the agent can read secrets, touch other projects or bypass the script validation by writing JSON directly.

resilience.name: OS-level Bash sandbox with whitelist fallback
resilience.what_it_is: Bash runs inside the SDK sandbox (bwrap on Linux, Seatbelt on macOS) with a network domain allowlist, kernel-level denyRead for sensitive paths, denyWrite for scripts/ and project.json, and allowUnsandboxedCommands=False. When no sandbox is available (native Windows) Bash is removed from allowed_tools and a default-deny can_use_tool callback only permits ffmpeg, ffprobe and skill scripts under .claude/skills/<skill>/scripts/, rejecting shell metacharacters and .. path segments. Every denied tool call returns a hint text to the agent.
resilience.function_in_system: Wraps all Bash commands the agent issues, the one channel the path hook cannot inspect (e.g. echo > project.json, python -c). Contains the blast radius of arbitrary commands and blocks the agent from asking for an unsandboxed retry. Otherwise a single generated shell command can overwrite protected project files, exfiltrate data or run arbitrary code on the host.

resilience.name: secret env scrubbing for Bash
resilience.what_it_is: A PreToolUse hook on Bash rewrites every command to env -u <VAR> ... sh -c '<cmd>', unsetting the Anthropic and other provider credential variables plus any env var whose name matches API_KEY, AUTH_TOKEN, ACCESS_KEY, ACCESS_TOKEN, SECRET_KEY, CREDENTIAL or CLIENT_SECRET.
resilience.function_in_system: Sits on the Bash tool path when the sandbox is enabled. The SDK subprocess holds real Anthropic credentials and Bash inherits the parent env, so the agent could read keys via env or pass them to generated commands. Otherwise credentials leak into the agent context and transcripts.

resilience.name: human-in-the-loop via AskUserQuestion
resilience.what_it_is: The can_use_tool callback intercepts the AskUserQuestion tool, registers a pending question, pushes it to the frontend stream and awaits the user's answer future; answers are merged into the tool input. On interrupt or session close the pending question is cancelled and the call is denied with interrupt=True. The persona prompt instructs the agent to present options for uncertain creative decisions.
resilience.function_in_system: Pauses the agent loop inside a tool call until a human decides. Keeps the user in control of creative choices before the agent triggers expensive image and video generation. Otherwise the agent decides alone and wrong assumptions propagate into paid generation runs.

resilience.name: session concurrency cap and idle eviction
resilience.what_it_is: Before a new session starts, _ensure_capacity compares active sessions with agent_max_concurrent_sessions (default 5); at the limit the least recently active non-running session is evicted, and if all sessions are running the request is rejected with SessionCapacityError. Finished sessions are evicted after agent_session_cleanup_delay_seconds (default 300 s, min 10 s), and a patrol loop every 300 s evicts sessions idle for more than twice that delay.
resilience.function_in_system: Server level, around all agent sessions; each session holds its own Claude SDK subprocess. Bounds memory, process count and concurrent API usage. Otherwise sessions accumulate until the host runs out of resources.

resilience.name: stuck session recovery
resilience.what_it_is: Session creation waits at most 60 s (_SDK_ID_TIMEOUT) for the SDK session id while also watching the actor task, failing fast with cleanup if the actor dies. Eviction sends a disconnect with a 15 s budget and cancels the actor task on timeout. Sessions still marked running at close are persisted as interrupted, and on service startup all sessions left running in the DB are set to interrupted.
resilience.function_in_system: Session lifecycle around the agent loop. Handles a hanging SDK subprocess, a crashed actor and server restarts. Otherwise a session stays in status running forever, blocks new messages (send_message rejects running sessions) and keeps holding a concurrency slot.

resilience.name: session-bound MCP tools
resilience.what_it_is: Each agent session gets its own in-process MCP server built with project_name captured in a ToolContext closure; tools never take a project argument, and script arguments are validated to be bare filenames; path separators and dot segments are rejected.
resilience.function_in_system: The MCP tools run in the server main process outside the sandbox with DB and provider access. Binding them to one project contains the agent's actions. Otherwise a prompt injection or a hallucinated path can redirect generation and edits to another project or arbitrary files.

resilience.name: tool errors returned as observations
resilience.what_it_is: Every MCP tool handler wraps its body in try/except and returns tool_error(), a text result with is_error=True; batch tools also set is_error when some items failed and list each failure.
resilience.function_in_system: Return channel from the tools into the agent loop. The agent sees the error text as a tool result and can fix arguments, retry or report to the user. Otherwise an exception aborts the agent turn and the agent has no information to react to.

resilience.name: checkpoint resume for video batches
resilience.what_it_is: Episode and selection video tools write a checkpoint file (videos/.checkpoint_ep<N>.json or .checkpoint_selected_<hash>.json) with completed ids after every successful video. With resume=true the checkpoint is loaded and reconciled with the mp4 files on disk, and only missing items are enqueued; the failure message tells the agent to rerun with resume=true. The checkpoint is deleted after a complete run.
resilience.function_in_system: Inside the long-running video generation tools the agent calls. Video generation is the slowest and most expensive step, and batches can fail midway. Otherwise a rerun after a partial failure regenerates and pays for all videos again.

resilience.name: generate only missing items
resilience.what_it_is: When the agent passes no explicit ids, the generation tools select only items that still lack output: storyboards lacking generated_assets.storyboard_image and assets lacking a design image are selected, and video units whose mp4 already exists are skipped.
resilience.function_in_system: Default selection in the enqueue tools. Makes repeated tool calls idempotent. Otherwise each call regenerates and pays for already finished media.

resilience.name: per-provider concurrency limits

Providers whose pool is full are excluded in the claim SQL, so their tasks stay queued; a task whose provider does not support its media type fails immediately with a failure code.
resilience.function_in_system: Throttles the generation calls that the agent's batch tools fan out to third-party media providers. Keeps request rates within provider rate limits and quotas and avoids claim-requeue churn for saturated pools. Otherwise a large episode batch fires all image and video requests at once and runs into rate-limit errors and failed tasks.

resilience.name: bounded task wait with worker liveness check
resilience.what_it_is: enqueue_task_only refuses to enqueue while the worker lease is expired. wait_for_task polls the task status and raises TaskWaitTimeoutError after 3600 s or WorkerOfflineError once the worker lease has been missing for the grace period (at least 20 s, twice the lease TTL).
resilience.function_in_system: Sits inside the MCP generation tools, which block the agent's tool call until the queued generations finish. Turns a dead or stuck worker into a bounded error that returns to the agent as a tool result. Otherwise an agent turn hangs indefinitely on a task that no worker will ever process.

resilience.name: active task deduplication
resilience.what_it_is: A unique partial index over project, task type, resource id and script file for active statuses (queued, running, cancelling) rejects a second insert; enqueue then returns the existing task id with deduped: True.
resilience.function_in_system: At the queue entry used by the agent's MCP tools and the WebUI. Makes repeated enqueue requests for the same resource idempotent while a generation is still active, e.g. when the agent retries a tool call or the user clicks twice. Otherwise duplicate tasks generate and pay for the same image or video several times and race on the asset write-back.

resilience.name: dependency-gated claiming with failure cascade
resilience.what_it_is: A queued task with a dependency_task_id is claimable only after its dependency has succeeded. When a running task fails, all queued tasks depending on it are recursively marked failed with the message "blocked by failed dependency <id>: <error>".
resilience.function_in_system: Governs chained batches such as storyboards that use the previous frame as reference, enqueued by the agent's batch tools. A failure upstream terminates the downstream chain quickly and reports the root cause per item to the waiting tool. Otherwise dependent tasks wait forever for a dependency that never succeeds, or run with a missing reference and break visual continuity.

resilience.name: shared retry with exponential backoff and jitter
resilience.what_it_is: with_retry_async wraps provider calls with up to 3 attempts, backoff 2/4/8 s plus 0-2 s random jitter; it retries ConnectionError, TimeoutError and messages matching transient patterns (429, resource_exhausted, 5xx, timeout). Backends plug in their own predicates (gRPC status codes for Grok, OpenAI error classes, 4 attempts for OpenAI text). Result downloads use a more lenient profile of 5 attempts with 5-40 s backoff, since a failed download wastes no generation quota.
resilience.function_in_system: Wraps every image, video, audio and text provider call made by the generation worker and the agent's text generation tools. Absorbs transient provider and network failures inside a single task. Otherwise a rate-limit or gateway hiccup fails the task, and the agent sees an avoidable tool error or re-triggers a paid generation.

resilience.name: billing-safe submit retry policy
resilience.what_it_is: Separate retry predicates per request phase. Non-idempotent create/submit POSTs are retried only when the request provably never left the client (connect, pool or proxy errors) or the server returned 408, 425, 429 or 5xx; transport errors after sending (read timeout, broken connection) are converted by submit_post into AmbiguousSubmitError [create_ambiguous], which ends the task. Idempotent polling retries all transport errors and 404; deterministic 4xx and local protocol errors fail fast in every phase.
resilience.function_in_system: Sits inside the submit, poll and download steps of the HTTP media backends run by the worker. Distinguishes safe retries from retries that could create a second provider job. Otherwise an automatic retry after a lost response creates and bills the same generation twice, and retries on deterministic 4xx errors occupy a worker slot until max_wait.

resilience.name: bounded polling of provider jobs
resilience.what_it_is: poll_with_retry queries asynchronous provider jobs at a fixed interval, retries transient poll errors and raises TimeoutError after max_wait. Limits are set per provider: Ark 600 s (3600 s for the flex tier), Gemini 600 s, DashScope and MiniMax max(900 s, 60 s per video second).
resilience.function_in_system: Runs inside the video (and some image) generation tasks after submission, while the worker holds a provider slot. Turns a provider job that never finishes into a task failure. Otherwise a stuck job blocks its concurrency slot indefinitely and the agent's waiting tool call only ends at the one-hour wait timeout.

resilience.name: structured-output fallback cascade
resilience.what_it_is: Text backends first request native strict json_schema output. On a schema incompatibility error, or when the returned text fails strict validation against the Pydantic response model (proxies that ignore or loosely apply response_format), the call falls back to Instructor, which parses, validates and re-asks up to 2 times; dict schemas fall back to json_object mode. Token usage of the discarded native call is added to the fallback result. Ark sends models lacking registered structured-output support straight to the fallback path.
resilience.function_in_system: Sits inside the text generation calls behind the agent's normalize, script generation and episode planning tools. Keeps structured output reliable across many providers and OpenAI-compatible proxies. Otherwise schema-violating JSON reaches downstream Pydantic parsing as a raw ValidationError, or the step fails entirely on providers with partial structured-output support.

resilience.name: no-worse guard for project.json asset upserts
resilience.what_it_is: patch_project upserts characters, scenes and props inside the project file lock. The mutation validates the project payload before and after the change and raises before the atomic write when the change adds any new validation error; pre-existing errors pass. Only description and agent-editable fields are accepted, sheet paths and reference_image are dropped, and the result reports added, merged and dropped fields to the tool.
resilience.function_in_system: Single agent write path for project.json, complemented by the access fence that blocks direct Write/Edit on it. Protects the asset definitions that drive every sheet, storyboard and video generation, and the diagnostic return tells the agent which fields were ignored. Otherwise the agent can write structurally broken assets or overwrite pipeline-managed sheet paths, and repeatedly retries fields that are silently dropped.

resilience.name: manifest-driven agent profile sync
resilience.what_it_is: The agent profile (.claude/ and the mode-specific CLAUDE.md) is copied into each project under a manifest with sha256 per file, which separates untouched built-in files, user-modified files and user deletions (tombstones). A missing, corrupt, symlinked or mismatched manifest, or a changed content_mode, triggers a full reset from the profile; real I/O errors propagate.
resilience.function_in_system: Runs when a project is created or synced, before agent sessions load the project settings. Keeps the prompts, subagents and skills each session runs with consistent with the declared profile and the project's content_mode, while preserving deliberate user edits. Otherwise stale or locally corrupted prompt files steer the agent with wrong workflow rules.
